narration.text: Feed Control Lab: natural-language control of a short-video recommender, on real KuaiRec data, on this laptop.
A SASRec model trained on KuaiRec ranks the videos. The language model only proposes changes; I review them.
First, the original study. Condition C takes a free-text category instruction.
I name one category by its dataset ID.
Apply. The rule parser reads it, and the fixed policy boosts that category.
The ranking changed, and each card explains the boost.
Compare A to E shows all five conditions side by side.
Now the language controls.
The display is in English: machine-translated from the original Chinese, and labelled as such. One click shows the original.
On the right: this user's top ten from the trained model.
Provider: the OpenAI API.
Model: GPT five, the strongest model in my tests that needs only an API key.
A key pasted here is masked and kept in memory only. Here it comes from an environment variable.
Use this provider.
Workflow one, the reference: a manual category control. No model.
I search the KuaiRec categories.
Labels can be searched in English.
I pick Dance.
Show more,
strong.
Preview. A preview never changes the feed.
10 videos would enter the top ten.
Before
and after.
Apply changes exactly the reviewed set.
Applied. Each card names the control that moved it.
Undo restores the previous feed exactly.
Workflow two: a request in my own words, mapped to existing categories and tags.
I just ate, and do not want to be tempted by food.
No category name is used.
Interpret and preview.
The model reads the request and the list of existing labels. It sees no video text.
Next, the server checks that every label exists and that the quoted words are in the request.
The answer is back.
Proposal: show less category snack; show less category Food tutorial; show less topic tag Kuaishou kitchen; show less topic tag Homemade food. 1 model call, 14 seconds of model time, about 4 cents.
The review shows the model's reason, the server's checks, and the effect on the feed.
Apply.
Undo.
A second request, in another domain.
My cat is at the vet, and I cannot bear to see animals.
No category name is used.
Interpret and preview.
The model reads the request and the list of existing labels. It sees no video text.
Next, the server checks that every label exists and that the quoted words are in the request.
The answer is back.
Proposal: hide category Pets; hide category Pet daily record; hide category Pet dog; hide category Pet cat, and 21 more. 1 model call, 15 seconds of model time, about 4 cents.
The review shows the model's reason, the server's checks, and the effect on the feed.
Apply.
Undo.
Workflow three: a new category that KuaiRec does not have.
I describe it.
Plain English, no existing label.
Step one: propose a definition.
The model reads the description and this user's top forty videos.
It drafts a label and a definition, and cites example videos with exact quotations.
The answer is back.
A label, a definition with conditions, and 3 cited examples, each quotation checked.
I review it, and rename the label.
When applied: show more.
Approve and classify.
Each video in scope is classified under the definition, ten per call, four calls in parallel.
Every match must quote the video's own text.
A separate call checks each quotation without seeing the verdict.
Only matches that pass both checks are selected.
Still waiting for the model, 21s so far.
The answer is back.
One row per video: verdict, quotation, independent check. 1 of 40 selected. 5 model calls, 63 seconds of model time, about 6 cents.
The feed stays visible on the right during review.
Apply. The new category is now a label of its own.
Workflow four: add a video that is not in KuaiRec.
A title
and
a description.
The model sees only these words.
Classify and preview.
The model assigns existing categories and tags, and judges the new category with a quotation.
Still waiting for the model, 8s so far.
It got existing categories and tags, and a checked verdict for my new category.
Apply. It starts at a cold-start score, since the model has no history for it.
Undo
and undo again.
Last control: auto-apply.
With it on, a preview is applied as soon as it arrives.
Preview,
and it is already applied.
I turn it off
and undo.
The Results page reads the measured result files.

The first table is the nonliteral requests. Exact means the right action, every required label, and nothing outside the reviewed acceptable set. Claude Sonnet five point five 17 of 20; GPT five 17 of 20; GPT five mini 16 of 20.
Next, cases where the model should not change the feed. Correct abstentions: Claude Sonnet five point five 12 of 14; GPT five 10 of 14; GPT five mini 7 of 14.
For new categories, member F1 on the shared pool of one hundred fifty KuaiRec items: Claude Sonnet five point five 0.87; GPT five 0.92; GPT five mini 0.94.

Downstream, on the trained ranker, the controls raise the share of target videos in the top ten from almost zero toward the level of the reviewed control. The table and the non-inferiority test below give the exact numbers, including where the relative ten percent margin is not met.
The last table lists latency, cost and every failure of every model.
Below, the old parser bank is re-used, and labelled as re-use. Llama again scores seventy-nine, short of the eighty-five percent target.
The test set was drafted by an AI and reviewed row by row by me. Claude is both the drafter's family and a measured model.
Code, tests and results are in the repository. Thank you.
